why: SH695 — the one place the two regions readers are held to the same answer. `ShHtmlRegions` (Java, Jsoup, over the page the instance renders) and `cli/src/regions.mjs` (JavaScript, a tag stack, over the HTML the replica serves) are two implementations of one judgement, and a shared implementation is not available: the CLI declares no third-party dependency and adding an HTML parser to gain this would be the first. So they agree by assertion instead. Both suites read this file — ShHtmlRegionsAgreementTest and regions.test.mjs — and a case added here is a case both must answer.
rule: Each case's `expect` is the landmarks in document order, as `<tag>:<markup>`. Keep the awkward shapes: bad nesting and raw text are where two parsers disagree, and a fixture set of neat pages proves the readers agree about the pages that were never going to be a problem.

cases.name: chrome kept, sections authored — the replica's own shape
a landmark nested inside an authored section belongs to the section
data-shio-section marks a section too, and on the element itself
the marker does not leak past its close tag
a void element opens no frame
HTML is not XHTML: a trailing slash does not close a section, so the footer is inside it
markup inside a script is text, not structure
an unclosed paragraph does not take its section's frame with it
a close tag matching nothing closes nothing
a page with no landmarks at all
